sections.h2: Should a Strongsville owner list the house or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
The answer turns on timing and condition. A house in good order can draw a strong price on the open market, while one that needs work or sits in an estate may sell faster to a buyer who skips the repair list. About 82 percent of Strongsville homes are owner-occupied, so most sellers here are weighing a move out of a house they have lived in for years.

  • Agent listing: exposure to Cleveland-area buyers, with inspection and appraisal hurdles still ahead.
  • Owner-run sale: you skip the commission and take on the marketing, contract and disclosure work.
  • As-is cash purchase: one negotiation, no staging, and a closing date you help choose.

Each of these paths ends with a deed presented to the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Strongsville?
sections.html:
Strongsville is a Cleveland suburb of 24.64 square miles in Cuyahoga County. It takes its name from John Stoughton Strong, who led settlers here in 1816, and the township was officially organized on February 25, 1818. Village status came in 1923, followed by city status in 1961.

Locals call it the Crossroads of the Nation, a name that started where a railroad met an electric line between Cleveland and Wooster. The motto and seal now refer to Interstate 71 and the Ohio Turnpike, which cross inside the city. Highway access is an easy point to feature in a listing.

The Rocky River's east branch enters from North Royalton, and Cleveland Metroparks manage its banks as Mill Stream Run Reservation, with Bonnie Park and Ranger Lake. RTA buses serve the city. Southpark Mall and the Strongsville Business and Technology Park, which Wikipedia calls the largest industrial park in Northeast Ohio, sit among the major commercial sites.

sections.h2: Who lives in Strongsville, and who buys there?
sections.html:
Strongsville's median age was 45.8 in 2020, and nearly a quarter of residents were past 65. Married couples headed 58.2 percent of its 18,643 households, and 26.0 percent lived alone. Of 19,406 housing units, 3.9 percent were empty.

That profile suggests plenty of owners who have stayed put a long time. When they downsize or an estate settles, an outdated kitchen, bath or mechanical system may be easier to sell as-is than to renovate. Buyers are well educated, with 48.3 percent of adults holding a bachelor's degree or more, and the mean commute is 25.5 minutes.

sections.h2: Which Strongsville schools and parks matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Strongsville City Schools has five elementary buildings (Chapman, Kinsner, Muraski, Surrarrer and Whitney), a middle school on Pearl Road and a high school on Lunn Road. Allen, Drake and Zellers elementary schools have closed as enrollment fell. St. Joseph and John's is a Catholic school through eighth grade.

A bond issue of $81 million passed in 2012 and paid for a combined middle school, high school renovations and technology upgrades, with the new middle school ready for 2016-2017.

  • Town Center Park, opened in 2024, with a pavilion, playgrounds and courts.
  • Strongsville Commons and the Clock Tower, site of the Homecoming and the Rib Burnoff.
  • Gardenview Horticultural Park and the Freedom Trail veterans memorial.

sections.h2: What does the Strongsville Building Department handle?
sections.html:
Permits, contractor registration, business licensing, inspections and code compliance all run through the office at 16099 Foltz Parkway. It keeps weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., accepts online submissions through its portal around the clock, and answers at 440-580-3105.

The city lists additions, decks, fences, sheds, roofs, windows and doors, pools, electrical, plumbing, HVAC and garages as permit work. A contractor has to register with Strongsville before a permit can be issued, and a homeowner permit covers only labor the owner performs. Book inspections at least a day ahead.

Property maintenance inspections happen in the warmer months. Inspectors walk streets on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and carry a city photo ID. Clear any violation notice before you list, since a buyer's agent or title company is likely to ask.

sections.h2: How does a deed transfer through the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office?
sections.html:
Cuyahoga County's Fiscal Officer took over the work of the old auditor, recorder and engineer offices. A deed needs one of two forms: the DTE 100 statement of value, or the DTE 100 EX when an exemption from the conveyance fee applies. The county's standards say a standard instrument normally takes three business days to review and must list the parcel number and site address.

  • Recording: $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after, effective October 24, 2024 under Senate Bill 94.
  • Transfer tax: a county may levy up to thirty cents per hundred dollars (Ohio Revised Code 322.02), paid by the grantor before recording.
  • Rate: ask the Fiscal Office or your closing agent which conveyance rate Cuyahoga County applies today.

The division answers at 216-443-2060. Heirs can read its Great Estates Program for ways to avoid delay and cost, and owners can sign up for Property Alerts about suspicious filings against their parcel.

sections.h2: Which Strongsville sellers are exempt from the Ohio disclosure form?
sections.html:
The state form under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 has exemptions. A person who inherited the house and did not live in it during the prior year is excused, and so are estate fiduciaries, transfers to a spouse or lineal relative, foreclosures and court-ordered sales.

A seller who is covered must deliver the signed form to every buyer promptly. If the form arrives after a contract exists, the buyer has three business days from receipt to rescind in writing, and the window closes 30 days after acceptance or at closing if that comes first.

faqs.q: Does Strongsville require a point-of-sale inspection?
faqs.a: The department describes permit inspections and summer property maintenance checks. Call 440-580-3105 to ask what applies to your address and whether any permits are still open.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Cuyahoga County?
faqs.a: Cuyahoga County lists $39 for two pages plus $8 per additional page, a change that took effect October 24, 2024. The conveyance charge is a separate line, so request the current figure when you book the closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the Cuyahoga County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: The grantor, which means you as the seller. The statute sets the ceiling at thirty cents per hundred dollars, and the county decides what it actually levies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Strongsville house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, after whoever holds legal authority signs the deed. The county's Great Estates Program covers ways to avoid delay, and the state disclosure form is not required from a seller who inherited and never lived in the house.

faqs.q: Do I need a contractor to fix permit problems before selling?
faqs.a: Not always. A homeowner permit exists for work you do yourself at your own residence, but any portion handled by a contractor needs one who has registered with the city.
